library(haven)
X37990_0001_Data <- read_sav("ICPSR_37990/DS0001/37990-0001-Data.sav")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)

fed_sentence <- X37990_0001_Data %>% 
  select(USSCIDN,NEWRACE,MONSEX,AGE, CITIZEN, NUMDEPEN ,OFFGUIDE, CIRCDIST, XFOLSOR,DISPOSIT,PCNTDEPT,SUPERMAX, SUPERMIN, TOTPRISN )

fed_sentence <- fed_sentence %>% 
  replace_na(list(PCNTDEPT = 0))

      !is.na(SUPERMAX) &
        !is.na(SUPERMIN) &
        as.numeric(TOTPRISN) > as.numeric(SUPERMAX) ~ (((as.numeric(TOTPRISN)- as.numeric(SUPERMAX))/ as.numeric (SUPERMAX))*100),
      as.numeric(TOTPRISN) < as.numeric(SUPERMIN) ~ (((as.numeric(TOTPRISN)-as.numeric(SUPERMIN))/as.numeric(SUPERMIN))*100),
      TRUE ~ 0 #Entered code into ChatGPT and asked why it was throwing an error, helped me figure out how to use !is and case_when() https://chatgpt.com/s/t_6aac1c4d3f908191b56accf5c5d3fd61

sampled_fed <- ready_fed_sentence[sample.int(nrow(ready_fed_sentence), 2000),] #I originally had around 75,000 observations even after pulling out all the NAs and it made the box plots and graphs in general basically unreadable, so I decided to randomly sample a smaller amount of observations. https://www.learningtree.com/blog/randomly-sampling-rows-r/

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## How can we explain the variation in departure from sentencing guidelines in federal criminal court?

- Federal Guidelines: Provide structure while allowing for judicial freedom

  - Considers: offense, criminal history, mitigating or extreme factors

- Consistent rulings across regions, defendant demographics, and non-legal factors

## Federal Sentencing Data

- United States Sentencing Commission, DOJ

<!-- -->

- 574 variables, 76538 observations -\> 10 variables, 3000 observations

- Concerns:

  - recoding of variables and values

  - citizenship variable

  - sampling/size

  - attorney

## Variables

- Response Variable: Percent Departure from Federal Sentencing Guidelines (numeric)

- Explanatory Variables:

  - Defendant Characteristics

    - Numeric: Age, Number of Dependents

    - Categorical: Citizenship status, Race, Sex

  - Court Characteristics:

    - Numerical: Offense Level

  - Categorical: Offense, Region of Court, Disposition

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot(data = sampled_fed, aes (x = newrace_clean, y = per_change)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(color = newrace_clean))+
  facet_wrap(~region)+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-100,400))+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))+
  xlab("Defendant Race")+
  ylab("Departure from Sentencing Guidelines (%)")+
  labs(color = "Race/Ethnicity")+
  ggtitle("Relationship between Defendant Race and Departure from Sentencing Guidelines Across Regions")
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = sampled_fed, aes(x = XFOLSOR, y= per_change))+
  geom_smooth()+
  facet_wrap(~newrace_clean)+
  xlab("Offense Level")+
  ylab("Departure from Sentencing Guidelines (%)")+
  ggtitle("Relationship between Departure from Sentencing Guidelines and Final Calculated Offense Level Across Race")

```
